title: climate focus spain declares national emergency over wildfires 2026 07 24
text:
Today’s newsletter continues to focus on Europe’s raging wildfires after the Spanish government declared a national emergency on Thursday following a series of wildfires that threatened communities near Madrid.
More than 10,000 people have been evacuated in Spain’s capital and the neighbouring province of Avila as firefighters struggled to contain the blazes.
Under Spain's National Civil Protection System law, the declaration places the emergency under the ​direct authority of the interior minister, who is responsible for coordinating the response. Authorities said it was the first such declaration linked to wildfire.
The Interior Ministry said the ‌decision was taken because of the simultaneous outbreak of several fires, adverse weather conditions and the need to mobilize extensive resources from different public administrations, increasing the complexity of firefighting and civil protection efforts.
Spain and much of southern Europe face increasingly severe wildfire seasons that scientists have linked to climate change.
Over in France, more than 10,000 people were evacuated as a rapidly spreading wildfire ripped through at least 2,400 hectares of land west of the city of Bordeaux in the nation's southwest, ​officials said.
The prefecture said 500 firefighters were battling to control the blaze, adding that no one had been injured so far.
The wildfire is located near the Arcachon Bay area, a ​tourist hotspot, and many of those evacuated are visitors staying in camping sites. "Overnight, the fire spread more quickly than we had imagined," said Philippe de Gonneville, ⁠the mayor of Lège-Cap Ferret.
Experts say abundant vegetation growth following unusually heavy spring rainfall has dried out in extreme summer heat, creating fuel for rapidly spreading fires.

The death toll from a landslide in the southwestern Chinese city of Chongqing last week has risen to 11, with 50 people still missing and 10 injured, following torrential rain on July 17, China’s Xinhua news agency said. The confirmed death toll from the collapse of the mountainside previously ​stood at eight, with 34 reported missing.
China warned of heavy rain and severe flood risks as the third tropical cyclone this month, Storm Noul, tracked ​closer to the country's southern coast. As of Friday morning, Noul was northeast of Manila, the capital of the Philippines, and was forecast to move within 800 km (497 miles) of Hong Kong by the evening, according to the ‌city’s observatory.
The U.S. National Hurricane Center said that Tropical Storm Bertha had moved inland near the Texas-Louisiana border about 75 miles (121 km) from Galveston, Texas. The U.S. weather forecaster said the storm had maximum sustained winds of 45 miles per hour (75 kph), spreading heavy rain across portions of coastal Texas.
Scientists are preparing to launch the first outdoor tests of genetically modified screwworm flies, in an effort to develop a more effective weapon against the flesh-eating parasite that has spread through Central America and into the United States. Number of the Week
$19.6 billion
That’s the amount of money that the World Bank estimates the two powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24 caused in direct physical damage. The lender said the cost of rebuilding ​could be twice as high or more after the quakes killed about 5,000 people, injured nearly 17,000 and left almost 18,000 homeless, while devastating homes, infrastructure and commercial buildings, including in Caracas.
